title: Manifest charge-transfer physics in T$^\prime$-La$_2$NiO$_4$
authors: Wiktoria Lewandowski, Steffen Bötzel, Ilya M. Eremin, Frank Lechermann
abstract: The La$_2$NiO$_4$ compound stabilizes in nature in the so-called T structure with octahedral oxygen coordination of the Ni site. Motivated by a similarly existing polymorph for La$_2$CuO$_4$ in the cuprate system, we here study La$_2$NiO$_4$ in the T$^\prime$-structure with square-planar oxygen coordination of Ni by means of first-principles many-body theory. The hypothetical T$^\prime$-La$_2$NiO$_4$ compound turns out to be a manifest charge-transfer insulator with a cuprate-like charge gap of $\sim 1.8$ eV. Upon doping, a strong carrier asymmetry is revealed, i.e. while holes dominantly enter O$(2p)$-derived states, electrons may become itinerant majorly within effective Ni-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ states. Nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic ordering at stoichiometry appears absent in the T$^\prime$ structure, in stark contrast to the strong antiferromagnetism in the T structure. Our theoretical study opens up new pathways for correlation physics in layered nickelates with challenging charge-transfer signatures, awaiting experimental inquiries.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the electronic structure of a hypothetical nickelate polymorph, T'-La2NiO4. Using advanced many-body techniques, the authors predict it is a charge-transfer insulator analogous to cuprates. The work details how doping affects carrier localization between oxygen and nickel orbitals, providing new insights into correlated layered materials.
main_problem: The study investigates charge-transfer physics in the hypothetical T'-La2NiO4 polymorph, drawing parallels with established cuprate superconductors.
main_result: The T'-structure is predicted to be a manifest charge-transfer insulator with a cuprate-like gap of ~1.8 eV, exhibiting doping-dependent carrier asymmetry between O(2p) and Ni-d states.
method: First-principles many-body theory calculations incorporating correlation effects via the DFT+SIC-DMFT approach were employed.
model_or_system: The system is single-layer nickelate oxide, La2NiO4, modeled using a five-orbital Slater-Hamiltonian parameterized by Hubbard U and Hund exchange J. It compares the T' structure to the bulk T structure.
key_observables: Charge gap energy, local orbital occupations (Ni 3d), spectral functions (projected vs. local), and magnetic ordering moments.
important_parameters: Correlation strength (U), charge transfer energy (Delta), doping level ($\delta$), and temperature ($T=200$ K).
main_assumptions: The use of DFT+SIC-DMFT formalism to capture strong electronic correlations, and the comparison relies on structural analogies with known cuprates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate crystal structures, band dispersions showing orbital contributions, Fermi surfaces for doped states (hole/electron), and magnetic moments comparing T vs. T' structures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical motivation by comparing to cuprates, details the theoretical framework using DFT+DMFT, presents results on charge-transfer insulating nature and doping asymmetry, and contrasts the magnetic ordering between the two polymorphs (T vs. T').
why_interesting: While focused on solids, the methodology of using DMFT/SIC to model correlated insulators with clear orbital differentiation is highly relevant for understanding strongly interacting quantum systems in general.
